root_cause_label: Agent correctly diagnosed interpreter mismatch (fasttext works only under /usr/local Python 3.13) but violated the task requirement by creating a wrapper script invoking /usr/local/bin/python3 instead of installing fasttext for the default system-wide interpreter (/usr/bin/python3 -> 3.11); the correct fix of running '/usr/bin/python3 -m pip install fasttext' was never attempted.
one_sentence_failure_summary: After confirming fasttext works under Python 3.13, the agent created a non-compliant wrapper script pointing to /usr/local/bin/python3 rather than installing fasttext for the required default system-wide interpreter (/usr/bin/python3, Python 3.11).
t_err_evidence: create wrapper run_with_fasttext.sh using /usr/local/bin/python3, bypassing the default system interpreter requirement
t_commit_evidence: Once the wrapper is created at step 17 and validated at step 19, the agent's subsequent behavior (steps 20-25: repeated pip calls to wrong interpreter; step 29: explicit decision to recommend Python 3.13; step 30: completion claim citing wrapper) shows the failing outcome was locked in at step 17.
t_surface_evidence: python3 -c "import fasttext" -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fasttext_pybind'
trigger_explanation: The task requires fasttext to be importable via the default system-wide python3 interpreter. The agent understood this requirement (step 29 explicitly states 'the user wants to use fasttext with the default system-wide python interpreter') but chose to bypass it by creating a wrapper pointing to a different interpreter (/usr/local/bin/python3 -> Python 3.13). The agent never attempted the compliant fix of '/usr/bin/python3 -m pip install fasttext'.
forewarning_evidence: PYTHONPATH hack: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fasttext_pybind'
